document.title: Request for Proposals: Security Camera System Replacement and Expansion
document.association_legal_name: Canyon Gate at Cinco Ranch Owners Association, Inc.
document.issuer: Bedrock Association Management, on behalf of the Association

project.summary: The Association is replacing and expanding its common-area video surveillance system at four locations: the Club House, the Guard Shack, the Basketball Pavilion and the Back Entrance Gate. The system covers 27 cameras: 13 existing cameras to be reused, 6 cameras to be replaced and 8 new cameras. The Association will purchase and own the equipment, have it professionally installed, and view live and recorded video remotely. The Association does not want an active monitoring service. Several existing cameras are not working, so installation timing matters.

board_requirements.text: The Association purchases and owns the equipment.
Live and recorded video available remotely.
No active monitoring, and no recurring monitoring fees unless a required function cannot be provided separately.
Cameras are down; installation timing matters.

sections.title: Instructions to bidders
body: Canyon Gate at Cinco Ranch Owners Association, Inc. (the Association) requests proposals to replace and expand its common-area security camera system. Every bidder receives the same scope, camera schedule, pricing form and compliance matrix so the Board can compare responses on the same basis.
items: Attend the required site walk before submitting. Pre-existing faults, power needs and pathways observed at the site walk must be priced in the bid, not left to change orders.
Submit questions in writing by the question deadline. Answers are shared with every bidder.
Complete the pricing form exactly as provided. Enter 0 for any line that does not apply; do not leave a line blank.
Answer every line of the compliance matrix with Comply, Exception or Not Applicable, and explain every Exception and Not Applicable.
Return the full contract package listed in this RFP with the bid. A bid without the contract documents cannot be evaluated.
Pricing must remain valid for at least 60 days after the response deadline.

The Association may accept or reject any bid, waive minor irregularities, and ask any bidder for clarification. Submitting a bid does not create a contract. No work is authorized until a written contract is signed by the Association.

sections.title: Scope of work
body: Furnish, install, configure, test and hand over a complete, working video surveillance system covering the 27 camera positions in the camera schedule, with on-site recording, secure remote access, and full documentation and training.
items: Pre-installation site survey to confirm every camera position, mounting surface, cable path, power source and head-end location before equipment is ordered.
Reuse the 13 existing cameras identified in the schedule, after confirming each one works and is compatible with the proposed recording platform.
Replace 6 existing cameras and install 8 new cameras as listed in the schedule.
Replace the existing recorder with new recording servers and storage sized to the retention requirement.
Provide all mounts, back boxes, enclosures, switches, wireless or wired links, cabling, conduit, battery backup and lift equipment needed.
Program, aim and focus every camera; adjust views after installation; and re-aim the existing cameras where a better view is available.
Remove and dispose of replaced equipment, or turn it over to the Association if requested.
Deliver as-built documentation, administrator credentials, and training as described in this RFP.

sections.title: Camera-by-camera schedule
body: The camera schedule lists every camera position by location, with whether the camera is reused, replaced or new, what it must cover, and the minimum specification. Bidders must return the schedule with the make, model, resolution, lens and license assignment proposed for each position. Positions may be adjusted at the site survey only with the Association's written approval; the bid must still cover all 27 positions.

sections.title: Reused, replacement and new cameras
body: Reused cameras (13): 10 at the Club House and 3 at the Guard Shack. Replacement cameras (6): 4 at the Club House and 2 at the Guard Shack. New cameras (8): 3 at the Guard Shack, 3 at the Basketball Pavilion and 2 at the Back Entrance Gate.
items: The specification is not tied to any manufacturer. The make, model and firmware of the 13 existing cameras will be confirmed at the site walk.

Each bidder must state whether its proposed recording platform supports each reused camera, and how (industry-standard protocol or native integration). Reuse is the base bid only where support is confirmed.
If the proposed platform cannot support a reused camera, price its replacement as a separate alternate line. Do not drop the position.
Some existing cameras have faults. Bidders must test the reused cameras at the site walk and price any repair or replacement needed for them to work, rather than deferring it to a change order.

sections.title: Equipment specifications
body: Minimum performance requirements apply to every new and replacement camera. Equivalent or better products from any manufacturer are acceptable; state the make and model of each.
items: IP cameras powered over Ethernet, using H.265 or H.264 compression, with an industry-standard interoperability profile (for example ONVIF Profile S and T).
Minimum 4 megapixel resolution for general coverage cameras and minimum 8 megapixel (4K) for the wide-angle parking lot cameras.
Infrared night vision sufficient to cover each camera's field of view in darkness; state the rated infrared distance for each model.
Wide dynamic range for cameras facing bright openings, gates or headlights.
Exterior cameras rated at least IP66 for weather and IK10 for impact, with vandal-resistant housings and manufacturer-matched mounts or back boxes.

License plate cameras at the Guard Shack must capture a legible plate for vehicles in the gate lanes, day and night. State whether plate recognition software (a searchable plate log) is included, and whether it carries any recurring charge.
Equipment must comply with Section 889 of the 2019 National Defense Authorization Act. Identify the country of manufacture for each model.
All equipment new, in original packaging, with full manufacturer warranty registered to the Association.

sections.title: Servers and storage
body: Recording is on site, on servers the Association owns.
items: Provide recording servers or network video recorders at the head-end location or locations the bidder proposes (the baseline design uses one at the Club House and one at the Guard Shack). State the number of servers, usable storage after redundancy, drive type, and redundancy (RAID or equivalent).
Size storage to meet the retention requirement in this RFP for all 27 cameras at the recording settings stated in the bid.
Provide a battery backup unit (UPS) for each server and each network head-end, sized for orderly shutdown or at least 15 minutes of runtime; state the runtime.

Cameras with on-board recording, if proposed for any position, must still be viewable and searchable from the main video management software. State how footage is retrieved and how long it is retained on the camera.
Servers must be secured in a locked, ventilated location; identify any rack, cabinet or cooling the bidder will provide.

sections.title: Licensing
body: Every camera position must be recorded and viewable in the video management software, and licensing must be clear.
items: State the number of video management software licenses included and list which camera each license covers.
If any camera does not need its own license (for example a camera with built-in recording), say which cameras and why, and confirm it is still viewable and searchable in the software.
Licenses must be perpetual and registered to the Association. Any license that requires a subscription or annual renewal is a recurring charge and must be listed on the pricing form.
State the cost basis for adding cameras later, as a unit price per added license.

sections.title: Remote access
body: Authorized Association users must be able to view live and recorded video, search, and export clips remotely from a computer and a mobile app.
items: Remote access must not require opening inbound ports on the Association's network (no port forwarding).
Remote connections must be encrypted, and administrator accounts must support multi-factor authentication where the platform offers it.
Provide at least 5 named user accounts with role-based permissions (view live, view recorded, export, administer).
State the internet bandwidth needed at each head-end for remote viewing.
If remote access requires any subscription or recurring fee, list it on the pricing form as a recurring charge and identify it as remote access, not monitoring.

sections.title: Cloud access versus cloud storage
body: These are different services and must be priced separately. Cloud access means using a secure online relay or app to view the on-site system remotely. Cloud storage means recording or backing up video off site.
items: The base bid is on-site recording with secure remote access. Cloud storage is not part of the base bid.
If the bidder offers cloud storage, price it as an optional alternate and state the number of cameras, days stored off site, resolution and monthly cost.
For any cloud service (access or storage), state where the data is hosted, who can access it, how long it is kept, and what happens to the data if the service is cancelled.

sections.title: Expected retention days
body: The Association expects at least 30 days of continuous recording for all 27 cameras.
items: State the retention, in days, that the proposed storage achieves for all 27 cameras, and show the calculation: resolution, frame rate, compression, recording mode (continuous or motion) and storage per camera.
Price, as an optional alternate, the added storage needed for 60 days of retention.
Retention will be verified during acceptance testing.

sections.title: No active monitoring
body: The Association does not want an active monitoring service. The base bid must not include live monitoring, remote guard or video patrol, alarm response or dispatch, or any recurring monitoring fee.
items: Automatic system health notices sent directly to the Association (for example an email when a camera goes offline or a drive fails) are welcome if they are part of the software at no recurring charge. State whether they are included.

If a bidder believes a required function can only be delivered through a recurring service, the bidder must identify the exact function, explain why it cannot be provided separately, price that service separately, and identify a non-monitoring alternative.
Any recurring service the Association does not choose must not reduce the warranty or the system's ability to record, play back and provide remote access.

sections.title: Cabling, conduit and network
body: Provide every pathway needed to connect each camera to its recording server.
items: New Category 6 or better cabling for every new and replacement camera, terminated, labeled and tested. State the number of cable runs.

Conduit for exposed exterior runs, including the Basketball Pavilion cameras, any link to the Pavilion, and the Back Entrance Gate cameras. State the number and length of conduit runs and whether any trenching or boring is included.

Connectivity to the Basketball Pavilion: propose either a point-to-point wireless link (state both radios and the mounting locations) or a wired or fiber path. Provide an outdoor-rated enclosure with a hardened PoE switch at the Pavilion if the design needs one.
Back Entrance Gate: propose either a network connection to the head-end or on-camera or local recording with remote access. State which, and how footage is retrieved.
PoE switches at each head-end with enough ports and power budget for all connected cameras plus spare capacity; state port counts and budget.

The camera system must run on its own network segment (separate VLAN or physically separate switching) from any Association business or guest network. The Association will provide internet service at the head-end; state any requirement for it.

sections.title: Power assumptions
body: Do not assume power is available. Every power need must be identified and priced.
items: Identify every location that needs new 120-volt power, a new circuit, or a power supply, and either include it in the bid or price it as a separate line. A general exclusion for additional power is not acceptable.
If electrical work requires a licensed electrician or a permit, include it and say who performs it.
Exterior equipment must have surge protection; state what is provided.

sections.title: Change-order controls
body: The bid is a fixed, not-to-exceed price for the full scope after the site walk.
items: Conditions visible or testable at the site walk, including faults in existing cameras, wiring or power, are the bidder's responsibility to price in the bid.
Change orders are allowed only for conditions that could not reasonably be discovered at the site walk, or for scope the Association adds.
No change-order work may start without the Association's written approval of the scope and price before the work is done.
State unit prices now for likely additions: an added camera installed, an added cable run, an added conduit run per foot, an added license, and the hourly labor rate.

sections.title: Warranties
body: Warranty terms must be stated in the bid and must not depend on buying a maintenance or monitoring plan.
items: Installation workmanship warranty of at least 1 year from final acceptance, covering parts and labor, including trip charges.
State the manufacturer warranty for each camera, server, drive and switch model, and whether advance replacement is available.
State the warranty response time from a reported failure to on-site repair.
Warranty applies to the 13 reused cameras only if the bidder chooses to warrant them; state which reused cameras, if any, are warranted.

sections.title: Optional support and maintenance
body: Support and maintenance after the warranty is optional and must be priced separately from the base bid.
items: Describe exactly what an optional plan includes (remote support, on-site visits, firmware updates, inspections, loaner equipment) and what it excludes.

State the price, the term, whether it renews automatically, the notice needed to cancel, and any price increase on renewal. The Association will not accept automatic renewal without written renewal by the Association.
Any monitoring or alerting by the bidder bundled into a plan must be identified as such and priced separately where possible.
State hourly rates and trip charges for service outside any plan.

sections.title: Ownership of equipment, data and administrator credentials
body: The Association owns the system and everything it records.
items: Title to all equipment passes to the Association on payment. No equipment is leased, rented or provided as a service.
All recorded video, images, plate data, logs and configuration belong to the Association. The bidder may not use, sell or share them.
At acceptance, the bidder delivers the master administrator credentials for every server, camera, switch, wireless link and software account, and all license keys registered to the Association.
The bidder may keep a separate, named technician account only with the Association's written approval, and the Association may disable it at any time.
The system must keep working, recording and providing remote access if the Association ends any relationship with the bidder.

sections.title: Cybersecurity and privacy
body: The system must be installed and handed over in a secure state, and must respect residents' privacy.
items: Change every default password; use unique strong credentials for each device; disable unused services.
Update all firmware and software to the current stable release before acceptance and document the versions installed.
Encrypted remote access with no inbound ports opened; multi-factor authentication for administrators where supported; audit logging of user access and exports.
Bidder remote access to the system only with the Association's approval, through named accounts.
No camera may view into a private residence, back yard or window. No audio recording unless the Association approves it in writing.
Recommend and, if requested, price camera-surveillance signage at the covered areas.

Disclose any cloud service, data hosting location and subcontractor that would handle Association video, and notify the Association within 72 hours of any security incident affecting the system or its data.

sections.title: Insurance and licensing
body: Every bid must include a current certificate of insurance and the bidder's Texas license.
items: Commercial general liability of at least 1,000,000 per occurrence and 2,000,000 aggregate.
Business auto liability of at least 1,000,000 combined single limit.
Workers' compensation at statutory limits, with employer's liability.
Umbrella or excess liability of at least 1,000,000 is preferred; state the limit carried.
The certificate must name Canyon Gate at Cinco Ranch Owners Association, Inc. and its managing agent as additional insured on the general liability and auto policies.
Provide the bidder's Texas Department of Public Safety Private Security Bureau license number for installing security systems.
State whether any part of the work will be subcontracted, to whom, and confirm subcontractors carry the same insurance.

sections.title: Contract terms
body: Submit the complete contract the bidder would ask the Association to sign. The Association's counsel will review it before any contract is signed.
items: State the payment schedule. The Association prefers payments tied to equipment delivery and completed work, with at least 10 percent held until final acceptance.
No automatic renewals of any recurring service without written renewal by the Association.
No credit card or convenience fees; state accepted payment methods.
State any limitation of liability, indemnity and termination provisions. The Association will review them with counsel.
Texas law governs. The contract must be with the Association, signed by an authorized officer of the Association.
A completed IRS Form W-9 is required from the selected bidder before payment.

sections.title: Installation schedule
body: Several cameras are down, so the installation date is a deciding factor.
items: State the earliest installation start date after contract signing, equipment lead times, and the number of working days to complete.
The Association's target is to start installation on or before Monday, December 7, 2026, and reach substantial completion by Friday, December 18, 2026. Bidders who can start earlier should say so.
Optional alternate: describe and price any interim step to restore recording at the Guard Shack and the gate before the full installation.
Work at the Guard Shack must keep the gate operating and coordinate with gate staff. Work at the Club House and Pavilion must be coordinated with amenity hours.
Keep the working existing cameras recording until each one is cut over, wherever possible.

sections.title: Testing and acceptance
body: The system is accepted only after a documented test with the Association's representative and the Association's written acceptance.
items: For every camera: live view, recording, playback, export, night view and correct aim, with a saved snapshot of each view.
License plate cameras: legible plate capture for vehicles in the gate lanes in daylight and at night.
Remote access tested from off site on a computer and a mobile device, with each user role.
Retention calculation confirmed against the installed storage and recording settings.
Battery backup tested at each head-end; health notices tested if included.
Deliver an as-built camera schedule (position, model, IP address, license, view), network diagram, credentials, warranty registrations and manuals.
Provide at least 2 training sessions for Association users and management.
Correct all punch-list items before final payment.

sections.title: Pricing
body: Complete the pricing form. Every bidder prices the same lines so the Board can compare responses directly. Monitoring is not part of the base bid.
items: One-time charges: equipment; installation labor; cabling and conduit; network equipment; servers, recorders and storage; software and licenses; freight; sales tax; permits; and any other one-time charge, itemized.
Every recurring charge, required or optional, listed separately with its monthly or annual amount, term and renewal terms.
Totals: base installed total, first-year total and five-year total, calculated as defined on the pricing form.
Alternates priced separately: replacement of any reused camera the platform cannot support, 60-day retention, cloud storage, interim restoration, optional support plan, and signage.

compliance_matrix.requirement: Bid covers all 27 camera positions in the camera schedule, complete and working.
Pre-installation site survey included before equipment is ordered.
Compatibility of each of the 13 reused cameras confirmed with the proposed platform; any incompatible camera priced as a replacement alternate.
Faults in reused cameras found at the site walk are priced in the bid, not deferred to change orders.
Every new and replacement camera meets the minimum specification for its position (make and model stated).
License plate cameras capture legible plates in the gate lanes day and night; plate software and any recurring charge disclosed.
All equipment complies with Section 889 of the 2019 National Defense Authorization Act.
On-site recording servers owned by the Association, with stated usable storage, redundancy and a battery backup for each server and head-end.
Any camera with on-board recording is viewable and searchable in the main video management software.
License count stated with the camera each license covers; any unlicensed camera identified and explained.
Licenses are perpetual and registered to the Association; any subscription license listed as a recurring charge.
Live and recorded video, search and export available remotely on computer and mobile, with no inbound ports opened.
At least 5 named users with role-based permissions; multi-factor authentication for administrators where supported.
Cloud access and cloud storage priced separately; cloud storage only as an optional alternate.
At least 30 days of continuous recording for all 27 cameras, with the calculation shown.
Base bid includes no active monitoring and no recurring monitoring fee.
Any recurring service claimed as required identifies the exact function, why it cannot be provided separately, its separate price, and a non-monitoring alternative.
All cabling, conduit, wireless or wired links, enclosures and switches needed are included, with counts and lengths stated.
Camera system on its own network segment, separate from Association business or guest networks.
Every new power need identified by location and included or priced; no general exclusion for additional power.
Fixed, not-to-exceed price after the site walk; change orders only for undiscoverable conditions or added scope, with written approval before work; unit prices stated.
At least 1-year parts and labor workmanship warranty from acceptance, not conditioned on any service plan; manufacturer warranties stated.
Any support or maintenance plan is optional, priced separately, and does not renew without written renewal by the Association.
Association owns all equipment, recorded data and configuration; master administrator credentials and license keys delivered at acceptance.
System keeps recording and providing remote access if the Association ends any relationship with the bidder.
Default passwords changed, firmware current at acceptance, encrypted remote access, audit logging, and incident notice within 72 hours.
No views into private residences or yards; no audio recording without written Association approval.
Certificate of insurance meeting the stated limits, naming the Association and its managing agent as additional insured; Texas Private Security Bureau license provided.
Complete contract documents submitted; payment schedule tied to delivery and completion with at least 10 percent held until acceptance; no convenience fees.
Earliest start date, lead times and duration stated; able to start on or before December 7, 2026.
Documented acceptance test, as-built documentation, credential handoff and at least 2 training sessions before final payment.

rules: Enter every amount in US dollars. Enter 0 for a line that does not apply.
Sales tax is its own line. Do not include tax in other lines.
Base installed total equals the sum of all one-time lines, including sales tax.
First-year total equals the base installed total plus 12 months of every recurring charge marked required.
Five-year total equals the base installed total plus 60 months of every recurring charge marked required.
Optional recurring charges and alternates are listed separately and are not included in the three totals.
Monitoring is not in the base bid. A recurring charge that includes monitoring is never counted in the totals, even if marked required.

clarification_items.text: State the number of video management licenses included, list which camera each license covers, and explain any camera that is not separately licensed (for example a camera with built-in recording).
Confirm the make, model and firmware of the 13 existing cameras at the site walk, and whether the proposed platform supports each one.
Identify every location needing new power, and state whether it is included in the bid.
State the retention days achieved for all 27 cameras and show the calculation.
State the earliest installation start date, equipment lead times and working days to complete.

Confirm coverage is limited to the Club House, Guard Shack, Basketball Pavilion and Back Entrance Gate. Earlier proposals also covered the Rec Center, the resident exit, Tranquility Park and the South Gate; those are not in this RFP unless the Board adds them.

clarification_items.text: Confirm the 30-day retention target, with 60 days priced as an option.
clarification_items.source: Board requirement: appropriate storage and retention

Confirm the insurance limits and the 10 percent amount held until acceptance.
Decide whether to ask bidders to price an interim step to restore recording at the Guard Shack and the gate before the full installation.

Baseline proposal says 'a pair' of point-to-point stations on page 3 but itemizes quantity 1 on page 4 (stored line item marked uncertain). The RFP asks every bidder to state both radios.

Conflict-of-interest check before bidders are selected: one competing design on file lists a business development contact with the same name as the person the baseline proposal is addressed to. Management to confirm whether a disclosure is needed. Not raised with the Board or any vendor yet.
Confirm the site address and submission inbox printed on the RFP before it is issued, and that responses will be filed to this RFP record.
Existing vendor record 498a15b3 (ITECH MONITORING INC.) is deliberately not linked to this RFP. Do not create or link vendor records until a response is received.

If issue slips past October 22, keep the deadline 14 days after issue and tell the Board the installation start may move.
